standard_prerequisites.name: Tensor-restrict adjunction for sheaves of modules: Hom_{O}(O tensor_{f^{-1}f_*O} f^{-1}G, F) = Hom_{f^{-1}f_*O}(f^{-1}G, F_{f^{-1}f_*O})
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the first equality of the chain.

standard_prerequisites.name: Push-pull adjunction for modules: Mor_{Mod(f^{-1}f_*O)}(f^{-1}G, F) = Mor_{Mod(f_*O)}(G, f_*F)
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the second equality of the chain.

core_obligations: The tensor product O tensor_{f^{-1}f_*O} f^{-1}G is formed via the canonical map f^{-1}f_*O -> O, with the module structures on f_*F and f_*F as an f_*O-module supplied by the pullback and pushforward module constructions (statement lines 3196-3200). The tensor-restrict adjunction gives Mor_{Mod(O)}(O tensor f^{-1}G, F) = Mor_{Mod(f^{-1}f_*O)}(f^{-1}G, F_{f^{-1}f_*O}) (proof lines 3205-3211, justified at 3212-3213). The push-pull adjunction for sheaves of modules identifies the latter with Mor_{Mod(f_*O)}(G, f_*F) (proof lines 3211-3213, justified at 3213-3215). Chaining gives the asserted bijection, bifunctorial in G and F (proof lines 3203-3216).
proof_roadmap: Apply the tensor-restrict adjunction to move the tensor into the second argument (proof lines 3205-3213).
Apply the push-pull adjunction to land in Mor_{Mod(f_*O)}(G, f_*F) (proof lines 3213-3215).
